frozenDecisions: Capability authenticity is process-local object identity in Broker-private WeakMaps; serializable fields are not authority.
Authentic contexts are never exposed to Providers, HTTP clients, persistence, arguments, logs or general executors.
Tool authority binds immutable registration ID, executor identity, schema digest and policy digest rather than name alone.
Provider definitions and dispatcher execution derive from the same authentic frozen binding snapshot.
The current shared Agent/runtime is single-flight until RT-01; a second root run is rejected before memory mutation.
Persisted Session persona_name must match the effective Persona; missing Personas never fall back silently.
Persona, Settings, Session and runtime transitions revoke old authority before publishing new state.
SubAgent and Playbook contexts only attenuate pinned bindings, roots, network and all risk classes; no grants inherit.
Supervisor is advisory and Agent principals cannot change its state.
Approval challenge and grant are both exact, random, expiring, one-use and bound to session/run/binding/arguments.
Every Terminal operation and file reveal use a controlled direct-operation facade; Terminal resources are Session-owned.
Path canonicalization, executor sandboxing, genuine UI gesture proof and durable audit storage remain SEC-02/03/04/06.
implementationBatches: Persona digest, explicit network envelope and persisted Session binding
Immutable static/runtime registration bindings and collision rejection
Context-mandatory definitions/dispatcher and strict frozen argument validation
Agent run-local context and structured approval flow
SubAgent/Playbook attenuation and owned control resources
Terminal/file-reveal controlled facade, ownership and static boundary gate
31-scenario attack matrix, positive regressions and GOV-03/GOV-04 regression gates
externalDeferredBlockers: REL-01 approved Authenticode signer and RFC3161 timestamp
amendmentRule: Sections 3, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 12 cannot be weakened without a numbered Architect amendment before implementation changes.
